limbDarkening.source: Neckel H. (2005), Sol. Phys. 229, 13: analytical limb-darkening reference functions for 422-1100 nm, I(mu)/I(1) = sum_k A_k mu^k with A_k = c + l1/lambda + l5/lambda^5 (lambda in micrometres)

corona.source: Baumbach (1937) K+F corona, B(r)/B_sun = scale * sum a_i r^-p_i (r in solar radii, B_sun = mean disk brightness)

granulation.source: Typical solar values: granules ~1,000 km, lifetime ~10 min, white-light rms contrast ~14%; supergranules ~30,000 km (Nordlund, Stein & Asplund 2009, Living Rev. Sol. Phys. 6, 2)

cycle.source: Sunspot number from SILSO (WDC-SILSO, Royal Observatory of Belgium): minYear, maxYear and maxSsn are the 13-month smoothed minima and maxima (display values; minYear also starts the butterfly). Cycle shape from Hathaway, Wilson & Reichmann (1994), Sol. Phys. 151, 177: R = maxSsn * s((t - t0Year) / bYears) / max(s), s(x) = x^3/(exp(x^2) - c), c = 0.71, with t0Year and bYears least-squares fitted to the SILSO annual means 1986-2025 and the smoothed minima (2.2 in Dec 2008, 1.8 in Dec 2019). Cycle 25 after 2025 and cycle 26 are estimates; cycles outside the table repeat the generic row every periodYears

butterfly.source: Hathaway D. H. (2011), Sol. Phys. 273, 221: mean emergence latitude ~28 deg * exp(-t / 90 months) from cycle start (Sporer's law); spread and limits approximate

rotation.source: Snodgrass H. B. (1983), ApJ 270, 288: sidereal rotation of small magnetic features omega = A + B sin^2(lat) + C sin^4(lat) (2.902, -0.464, -0.328 urad/s converted to deg/day); frame rate is the IAU WGCCRE W-dot of the Sun (sun.fixed)

spots.source: Typical sunspot-group properties: umbra ~5-30% of the quiet-Sun intensity in white light (darker in the core and in big spots; umbraIntensity per channel follows 4000 K / 5800 K blackbody ratios), penumbra ~75-85% (penumbraIntensity 0.7 is the mean of high-contrast bright and dark filaments, a little below the measured range so it still reads after tone mapping), penumbra/umbra radius ~2.4, spots without a penumbra (pores) below ~1.5-2 Mm radius, partial (one-sided) penumbrae up to ~2.5 Mm, neighbouring umbrae of one polarity sharing a common penumbra, groups 50-200 Mm long with a compact leading spot and a fragmented following polarity, Joy's-law tilt ~0.5 x latitude, Gnevyshev-Waldmeier linear area decay over days to weeks; SSN = 10 G + N, so groups on the whole Sun ~ SSN / 7.5 (Solanki 2003, Astron. Astrophys. Rev. 11, 153; Borrero & Ichimoto 2011, Living Rev. Sol. Phys. 8, 4; van Driel-Gesztelyi & Green 2015, Living Rev. Sol. Phys. 12, 1)

prominences.source: Prominences 10-120 Mm tall (a few reach higher), H-alpha (656.3 nm) dominated, a few times brighter than the inner corona in totality (~1e-5 of the disk; colour: H-alpha with H-beta and Ca II, little green); quiescent ones live weeks at filament latitudes 15-55 deg and are seen against the disk as dark filaments a few times longer than they are tall (Parenti 2014, Living Rev. Sol. Phys. 11, 1; Mackay et al. 2010, Space Sci. Rev. 151, 333). Counts and brightness factors are approximate

halpha.source: Look of narrowband H-alpha full-disk photos (deep red-orange disk, mild limb darkening, dark filaments, bright plage); not physical exposure: the disk-mean luminance is luminanceScale times the white-light disk mean so the red channel stays below clipping
